entities.summary:
ExxonMobil Corporation is an American multinational oil and gas corporation formed in 1999 through the merger of Exxon and Mobil — both descendants of John D. Rockefeller's Standard Oil Company, broken up by antitrust action in 1911. It is the world's largest publicly traded oil and gas company by market capitalization and among the most profitable corporations in history.

Standard Oil's descendants, including Exxon and Mobil, maintained technological leadership in oil refining, petrochemicals, and exploration through the 20th century. The 1989 Exxon Valdez tanker disaster in Alaska — releasing 11 million gallons of crude oil — became a defining environmental catastrophe that shaped environmental regulation and corporate liability globally. Exxon's internal climate research in the 1970s-80s accurately predicted global warming, but the company chose to fund climate denial campaigns instead, a pattern later documented by journalists and investigated by attorneys general.

ExxonMobil's lobbying against climate legislation and funding of skeptic organizations, while knowing privately that its products caused warming, became one of the most scrutinized examples of corporate deception in history. Despite these controversies, ExxonMobil generated $56 billion in profit in 2022 — its most profitable year ever — and continued expanding oil production, positioning itself against the energy transition while competitors invested in renewables.
